def is_nested(s):
    # A subsequence may skip characters, so we only need two '[' before two ']'
    # with both openings before both closings: pattern [ ... [ ... ] ... ]
    # Greedily pair earliest openings with latest closings.
    opens = [i for i, ch in enumerate(s) if ch == '[']
    closes = [i for i, ch in enumerate(s) if ch == ']']
    # Count how many pairs (open, close) can be formed with open before close,
    # pairing earliest opens with latest closes.
    pairs = 0
    j = len(closes) - 1
    for i in range(len(opens)):
        if j >= 0 and opens[i] < closes[j]:
            pairs += 1
            j -= 1
        else:
            break
    return pairs >= 2

# Tests
print(is_nested('[[]]'))            # True
print(is_nested('[]]]]]]][[[[[]'))  # False
print(is_nested('[][]'))            # False
print(is_nested('[]'))              # False
print(is_nested('[[][]]'))          # True
print(is_nested('[[]][['))          # True
